text_blocks.snippet: On January 6th, Congress meets to count the electoral votes from the previous presidential election and formally declare the winner. In 2021, this process was interrupted by a violent attack on the U.S. Capitol building by supporters of then-President Donald Trump who sought to prevent the certification of Joe Biden's victory. This event, known as the January 6th attack, is now a significant date in American history, highlighting issues of political polarization, election integrity, and the fragility of democratic institutions.

list.title: Formal Electoral Vote Count:
list.snippet: Traditionally, January 6th is the day when Congress gathers to officially count the electoral votes from each state and officially declare the winner of the presidential election.

list.title: 2021 Capitol Attack:
list.snippet: In 2021, this process was disrupted when a mob of Trump supporters stormed the Capitol building in an attempt to stop the certification of the election results.

list.title: Domestic Terrorism:
list.snippet: The attack was classified by the FBI as an act of domestic terrorism, with the goal of preventing the peaceful transfer of power.

list.title: Ongoing Investigations:
list.snippet: The events of January 6th continue to be investigated by both congressional and law enforcement bodies, with the goal of understanding the causes of the attack and holding those responsible accountable.

list.title: Political Polarization:
list.snippet: The attack has further deepened political divisions in the United States, with different interpretations of the events on January 6th contributing to the ongoing polarization.

list.title: Security Enhancements:
list.snippet: In response to the attack, security measures at the Capitol have been significantly enhanced for subsequent January 6th sessions, including the counting of electoral votes.
